quotes.text: Request to join the preview for custom fraud models.
Enter your email to request access.
Custom models require enough transaction history to train an effective model.
After deployment, a new Radar risk score that incorporates Stripe global intelligence and your custom signals is available.
We retrain the model as your product catalog, customer base, and fraud patterns change.

old_evidence.text: After deployment, a new Radar risk score that incorporates Stripe global intelligence and your custom signals is available.

findings: Both complete captures describe Radar's network baseline, merchant-specific structured payment metadata and enough transaction history for Stripe's onboarding assessment. Merchant sends signals, Stripe trains using global and merchant data, deployment makes a new custom-informed score available, and Stripe retrains as merchant and fraud patterns change.

November newly documents requesting access to the preview using an email. It is a request stage separate from onboarding assessment, model training and deployment. The documentation does not give acceptance criteria beyond evaluating sufficient volume or a numerical threshold, and does not establish an approval outcome, enrollment or general availability.

The metadata and potential precision/recall benefits are unchanged. Account age, verification and VIP flags, session activity, product category/value tier/shipping and internal risk examples are conditional suggestions. Keep independently documented guidance on sensitive metadata and avoid treating an example or expected benefit as an eligibility gate or measured improvement.
substantive_changes: The complete November 7 guide adds an explicit invitation to request preview access and a sample documentation-side email submission to the preview registration endpoint with slug `radar_custom_models_preview`. The May 10 guide contains no registration route. This is access-process evidence, independent of the unchanged model training behavior or rollout state.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve both May and November captures, onboarding volume review, combined signals, scoring available after deployment with no further integration change at that phase, and retraining as conditions evolve.
Retain the related Radar risk-factors guide and the source/concept/index/company navigation. Keep custom-model preview separate from Radar custom rules or plan names.
conflicts: The concept says the custom score automatically replaces the global one. Both captures only say a new score incorporating Stripe global intelligence and custom signals is available after deployment; they do not say the global score is universally replaced or what happens for out-of-scope traffic.

Current source says metadata on PaymentIntent objects and 'no extra code needed'. The guide requires structured metadata on payment objects and gives `PaymentIntent.metadata` as an example. The absence of additional merchant action applies once relevant metadata is sent, and no integration change applies to score availability after deployment. The company/index shorthand should retain those conditions.
unresolved_questions: Preview request approval, account/region/plan eligibility, attested volume thresholds, current preview rollout and exact score-selection or fallbacks are not established by either capture.

findings: Record November's documented preview access request and preserve requirement to attach appropriate metadata plus Stripe's volume evaluation. Clarify initial metadata integration versus score availability after deployment, and replace the concept's claimed global score replacement with the directly supported combined-score wording. Preserve both dated raws, Radar concept and risk factors routes and matched provider/company entries.

source_assessments.reason: Preview access routing is a substantive addition to otherwise stable onboarding and scoring guidance. The access boundary and restrained score semantics materially improve the existing source and reciprocal labels.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/custom-fraud-models, the May 10 capture at old raw lines 8-39 and the November 7 capture at new raw lines 9-52 establish the same merchant-specific model workflow. The business sends structured payment metadata and has enough history for Stripe's onboarding assessment. Stripe trains from merchant metadata and global fraud signals, makes a custom-informed Radar score available after deployment, and retrains as business and fraud patterns change. November alone documents an email request for preview access before any established deployment. source-stripe-radar-custom-fraud-models.md captures the original sequence, but needs the preview scope and should present `PaymentIntent.metadata` as an example rather than the only allowed object and no further integration change as a deployment-stage claim.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/custom-fraud-models, old raw lines 10-25 versus new raw lines 11-38 show the substantive November 7, 2026 addition of the email-based preview request, absent from the May 10, 2026 capture. Old raw lines 25-39 and new raw lines 38-52 preserve the model lifecycle and suggested input examples; numbered steps and Markdown table formatting are presentational. The preview access request establishes neither acceptance nor general availability. Preserve the qualified no-change-after-deployment statement and remove the unsupported automatic global-score replacement from the concept. Retain both raw captures and source-stripe-radar-custom-fraud-models.md reciprocal routes through the Radar concept, Stripe index and company page, and the separate risk-factor source.
